subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: core event contracts and schema

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these AI-safety event families as a versioned core diagnostics contract, with trusted-emitter provenance and export privacy rules treated as permanent API guarantees?
rationale: The choice establishes a security-sensitive core and future plugin/exporter contract; code review alone cannot decide which event semantics, trust levels, and privacy guarantees maintainers intend to support long term.

options.title: Approve a narrowed core contract
options.body: Keep the six event families in core, but require discriminated payloads, trusted provenance, bounded metadata, explicit redaction rules, and compatibility tests before merge.

options.title: Keep diagnostics generic
options.body: Decline a dedicated core taxonomy and expose only generic diagnostic/plugin seams so optional safety classifications remain plugin-owned.

options.title: Defer the taxonomy series
options.body: Pause the issue and dependent PRs until operators demonstrate a narrower initial event set and concrete exporter requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrowed core contract
recommendation.body: Keep the six event families in core, but require discriminated payloads, trusted provenance, bounded metadata, explicit redaction rules, and compatibility tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The diagnostics framework originates in their work, and the decision spans core product scope, schemas, privacy, and security policy.
